claims.text: The target materials are nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy alloys.
The target alloys exhibit significant configurational disorder.
The target alloys have stable microstructures under high-temperature conditions.
The proposed model incorporates local mass variance, strain fluctuations, and nanoscale phase features when screening alloy compositions.
Phonon conduction is dominant under the thermal-insulation-relevant test temperatures.
Local chemical disorder enhances phonon scattering.
Nanoscale precipitate formation can enhance phonon scattering.
Local variations in atomic mass and bonding environments cause enhanced phonon scattering.
Enhanced phonon scattering lowers phonon thermal conductivity.
Quantifying local disorder and microstructural features at the atomic level will improve prediction of phonon thermal conductivity relative to averaged-property methods.
The proposed model will improve selection accuracy by at least approximately 20% over baseline methods.
Current baseline prediction methods rely on average compositional or bond-energy descriptors and omit atomistic disorder and microstructural detail.
The predictive approach is applicable only to predominantly disordered refractory high-entropy alloys in regimes dominated by phonon heat transfer.
The approach may not apply when electronic or magnonic heat conduction is significant.
The approach may not apply when long-range ordering substantially reduces local disorder.
Directly coupled measurements of microstructural disorder and phonon transport in high-entropy alloys are limited.

contradictions.description: The predicted improvement is framed as at least 20% better predictive or selection accuracy, whereas the falsification rule operationalizes it as at least 20% lower mean thermal conductivity among selected alloys. Predictive accuracy and the thermal-conductivity level of selected candidates are different quantities.
